question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 1 Term 1: health and hygiene
question_mappings.coverage_link: Identifies handwashing and clean water and explains one health benefit of each, aligned to the cited Grade 1 health and body-care topic.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.1 Name two healthy things Nandi does and give one reason each is healthy. [4]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 1 Term 2: safety and safe conduct
question_mappings.coverage_link: Waiting for turns and responding safely to a fall connect to safety learning; the exact scenario is proposed for educator review.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.2 What does Nandi do to use the slide safely? Give one other safe playground action and explain how each action helps keep children safe. [4]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Personal and Social Well-being: care and help-seeking
question_mappings.coverage_link: Assesses age-appropriate safety and care while an adult responds, without rescoring the teacher call already stated in the scenario.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.3 Her friend falls. Name four safe things Nandi can do while getting help. [4]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 1 Term 1: healthy routines
question_mappings.coverage_link: Ordering hygiene, eating and play actions applies a healthy-routine sequence.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.4 Starting with washing hands, put these actions in a helpful order: wash hands, sit to eat, play with a ball, tidy the ball away. [4]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Personal and Social Well-being: care for others
question_mappings.coverage_link: Kind support of a classmate connects to social well-being; confirm this activity fits Grade 1 term coverage.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.5 Give one kind way to help a classmate, say what you would do, and explain how it would help. [4]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 2 Term 2 reading: understanding a short written story and answering questions
question_mappings.coverage_link: Retrieves the planting day, location, seed type and a label detail from the printed story.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.1 When and where did Class Two plant the bean seeds? What did Asha put by each pot? [4]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 2 Term 2 reading: answering questions about a short written text
question_mappings.coverage_link: Retrieves two plant-care actions plus the measuring tool and the observed day from the printed story.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.2 Name two things the class did to help the seeds grow. What did they use to measure the shoots, and when did two shoots appear? [4]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 2 Term 2 reading: answering questions about a short written text
question_mappings.coverage_link: Explains why the class uses dry soil as the watering cue: avoiding unnecessary water and giving plants needed care without overwatering.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.3 Give two reasons the class watered the pots only when the soil felt dry. Explain how this helped save water and keep the plants healthy. [4]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 2 language structures: plural forms
question_mappings.coverage_link: Applies Grade 2 plural forms and the verb to be in a simple present-tense sentence, with singular noun agreement and sentence punctuation.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.4 Change this sentence to describe one pot: 'The pots are near a sunny window.' [4]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 2 Term 2 writing: sentences with taught words and punctuation
question_mappings.coverage_link: Writes two simple sentences on a familiar plant-care topic and applies sentence punctuation.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.5 Write two sentences about how you would care for a class plant. [4]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 3 whole-number addition
question_mappings.coverage_link: Adds two collected quantities within the Grade 3 whole-number scope.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.1 How many bottle tops did the class collect altogether? Show your addition. [4]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 3 whole-number division and grouping
question_mappings.coverage_link: Uses the previous item total to model equal groups of six, calculates quotient and remainder consistently with the learner's carried-forward total, and reports bags and unused tops; award method and result credit for consistent follow-through.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.2 Use your total from Question 1.1 to put the bottle tops into bags of 6. Show a calculation or equal-groups drawing. State how many full bags you can make and whether any tops are left. [4]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 3 overview: patterns, functions and algebra
question_mappings.coverage_link: Completes an increasing number pattern, states its constant-addition rule, and extends the rule to a later term.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.3 Complete the pattern 5, 10, 15, __, __, state its rule and give the number that would be in the eighth position. [4]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 3 Term overview: length measurement
question_mappings.coverage_link: Subtracting a used length from a measured length uses Grade 3 length work.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.4 A ribbon is 35 cm long. Sipho uses 12 cm. How much remains? [4]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 3 overview: 2-D shapes
question_mappings.coverage_link: Identifies a square or rectangle from the Grade 3 CAPS list, describes its four straight sides, and gives an object with that flat shape.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.5 Name one 2-D shape with four straight sides and one object with that shape. [4]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 4 Term 2 multiplication of whole numbers
question_mappings.coverage_link: Calculates equal groups using Grade 4 whole-number multiplication.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.1 Calculate the total number of seedlings. Show a method. [5]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 4 Term 4 perimeter
question_mappings.coverage_link: Uses tape-measured side lengths and addition to find the garden perimeter, matching the Grade 4 measurement skill without requiring a perimeter formula.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.2 Learners measured the garden’s four sides with a tape: 8 m, 5 m, 8 m and 5 m. Add the four measurements to find the perimeter. [5]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 4 common fractions
question_mappings.coverage_link: Forms 48/192, simplifies by dividing numerator and denominator by a common factor, and checks that one quarter of 192 is 48.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.3 What fraction of the 192 seedlings is 48? Simplify it. Show how you simplify the fraction and check your answer. [6]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 4 Term 2 addition and subtraction of whole numbers
question_mappings.coverage_link: Uses a written three-digit subtraction with visible regrouping, place-value subtraction and an inverse addition check; marks now correspond to the requested calculation and verification steps.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.4 The class has 360 seeds and plants 145. Show the column subtraction, make any regrouping clear, and check your answer with addition. How many seeds remain? [7]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 4 Term 3 capacity/volume: solve a capacity problem and convert between millilitres and litres
question_mappings.coverage_link: Multiplies 250 mL by 8, then applies the Grade 4 CAPS relationship between litres and millilitres to express 2,000 mL as 2 L.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.5 Each seedling needs 250 mL of water. For 8 seedlings, show the multiplication and the conversion calculation. Give the total in millilitres and litres. [6]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 5 Term 2 processing materials: mixing sand, gravel, cement and water to make concrete
question_mappings.coverage_link: Identifies the four ingredients and concrete product named in the Grade 5 CAPS processing-materials example.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.1 Name the four materials mixed in the example and name the processed material they make. [5]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 5 Term 2 processing materials: recording and comparing properties before and after processing
question_mappings.coverage_link: Records observable properties of starting materials and set concrete, then compares before/after properties as required for processing materials.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.2 State what property information learners should record before mixing and after the samples set. Give two examples of properties to compare and explain why they record both stages. [5]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 5 investigation skills applied to processing materials: planning a fair comparison
question_mappings.coverage_link: Applies the Grades 4–6 fair-test skill to the CAPS concrete example by varying gravel amount, measuring counter support before cracking, and controlling other conditions.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.3 In the two-sample test, identify what is changed, what is measured and three conditions that should be kept the same. Explain why this makes the comparison fair. [6]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 5 investigation skills and processed material properties: predicting and evaluating results
question_mappings.coverage_link: Uses the Grades 4–6 predicting, investigating and repeating skills to evaluate a stated comparison of two processed concrete samples; no outcome is asserted in advance.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.4 Based on the planned test, predict which sample will support more counters, or predict that they will support the same number. Explain why your prediction is reasonable, state what result will count as evidence, and give one reason the result should be checked with repeated trials. [7]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 5 investigation skills: recording results, repeating trials and evaluating a processed material
question_mappings.coverage_link: Records and compares results from a repeatable processing-material test and recognizes the limit of extrapolating small-sample results to a full path.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.5 Give suitable results-table headings, including units where needed, for the gravel test. Then describe one way to keep the comparison reliable and one limitation of using small samples to choose material for a real path. [7]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 6 Term 2: self-management responsibilities
question_mappings.coverage_link: Assesses late video use, sleeping late, stopped play and tiredness using the Grade 6 Term 2 self-management topic; the memo ties one habit to its classroom effect.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.1 Identify Thabo’s late-night habit and the activity he has stopped joining. State one effect in class and explain how his habit may contribute to it. [5]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 6 Term 2: self-management and prioritising
question_mappings.coverage_link: Creates an ordered plan for responsibilities and rest.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.2 Suggest a realistic evening plan with a time for homework, a screen-free period before bed and one sleep-preparation activity. Put the activities in a sensible order and explain how the plan could support rest. [5]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 6 social responsibility and supportive relationships
question_mappings.coverage_link: The help-seeking response is a proposed application of social responsibility and care.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.3 What could Thabo say to his friend? Write a respectful I-statement that names how he feels and why, asks for specific support, and names a trusted adult he could approach if the problem continues. Explain why asking for support is responsible. [6]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 6 Term 2 physical education: fitness programme
question_mappings.coverage_link: Benefits and safe participation connect directly to the Grade 6 fitness programme and safety measures.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.4 Give two benefits of regular physical activity. Then suggest safe steps for Thabo's gradual return to football, including how to prepare, when to rest, and what to do if he feels unwell. [7]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 6 self-management and decision-making
question_mappings.coverage_link: Evaluates options and recommends one self-management strategy; educator to confirm explicit decision-making coverage.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.5 Suggest two realistic options Thabo could use to reduce late-night screen use. Give one benefit of each option, one possible difficulty with either option, and recommend one option using the scenario. [7]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Financial literacy: Income and expenses
question_mappings.coverage_link: Distinguishes a material used to make the fruit cups from a business expense while recognizing the fruit purchase is both; classifies the table fee as an expense for market selling space.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.1 Classify these four items—fruit bought, cups bought, table fee, and money received from cups sold—as a production input, business expense, sales revenue, or all categories that apply. Explain why the fruit and table fee fit their categories. [6]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Financial literacy: Income and expenses
question_mappings.coverage_link: Calculates income from units sold and the stated selling price.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.2 Calculate revenue from the cups sold. [6]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Financial literacy: Accounting concepts; Income and expenses
question_mappings.coverage_link: Uses the case outlays and sales income to distinguish a cash balance from profit when inventory remains.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.3 Calculate sales revenue and the cash remaining after the stated outlays. Explain why that cash balance alone does not establish profit. [8]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 7 financial literacy: income, expenses and profit; entrepreneurship and Entrepreneur’s Day stock decisions
question_mappings.coverage_link: Connects unsold inventory, next-market stock planning, sales revenue and profit to Grade 7 Term 2 income/expenses/profit plus Term 3 buying/selling/profit and Entrepreneur’s Day; the practical freshness/safety considerations remain a case application.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.4 Explain two reasons the six unsold cups matter for the next market day. Use case facts to recommend how many cups to make or buy, and address freshness or safety, waste, and why unsold stock is not sales revenue. [10]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Entrepreneurship: Starting a business
question_mappings.coverage_link: Supports a next-market-day decision with case income, costs and customer-demand evidence.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.5 Recommend one change for Lebo's next market day and support it with two calculations or facts from the case. [10]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 8 Term 1: peer influence and self-concept
question_mappings.coverage_link: Applies the Grade 8 Term 1 CAPS scope for friends and peers influencing self-concept, positive self-talk, and strategies to extend personal potential; assignment details are the original source-based scenario.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.1 Explain how pressure from a friend could affect the learner’s confidence in their own ability. Write one positive self-talk statement and give one action that would help the learner use their own ability on the assignment. [6]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 8 Term 1: self-motivation and personal potential
question_mappings.coverage_link: Milestones apply self-motivation and strategies to extend potential; a two-week assignment plan is proposed.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.2 Create a two-week plan with three milestones and one leisure period. [6]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 8 Term 3: decision-making process
question_mappings.coverage_link: Compares options using a decision-making process in the Grade 8 plan.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.3 Compare asking the teacher for help with copying a classmate's work. [8]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 8 Term 1: friends, peers and personal feelings
question_mappings.coverage_link: A respectful boundary applies peer relationships and self-concept; confirm communication scope.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.4 Write a respectful message to a friend explaining a boundary about copying while preserving the friendship. [10]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 8 Term 2/3: learning style and school performance
question_mappings.coverage_link: Help-seeking and monitoring progress connect to applying learning style and considering school performance; exact study-skills alignment needs educator confirmation.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.5 Recommend one help-seeking step and explain how the learner can monitor progress. [10]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 9 Term 1: reading/viewing for comprehension
question_mappings.coverage_link: Retrieves three explicit services plus the stopping location and weekly day from the Grade 9 reading stimulus.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.1 Name three services the van offers and state where it stops each Thursday. [6]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 9 Term 1: infer meaning and identify main ideas
question_mappings.coverage_link: Explains purposes and makes inferences from a non-fiction stimulus.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.2 Explain why the service records borrowed books and uses offline tablets. [7]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 9 Term 1: make inferences
question_mappings.coverage_link: Interprets the speaker’s statement using evidence from context.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.3 What does Naledi mean when she says residents help shape the route? [8]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 9 Term 1: sentence structure and conventions
question_mappings.coverage_link: Recasts a sentence while preserving meaning using sentence-structure skills.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.4 Rewrite 'The tablets work offline, so learners can use them even when the mobile signal is weak' as two sentences without changing its meaning. Preserve both facts and their cause-and-effect link; check grammar, capitals and punctuation, and do not add a new claim. [9]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 9 Term 1: evaluate text features and infer meaning
question_mappings.coverage_link: Evaluates the service using evidence and text features; paragraph writing is a proposed response format.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.5 In a short paragraph, evaluate one strength and one limitation of the travelling library service. [10]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 10 motion in one dimension: position and displacement
question_mappings.coverage_link: Uses a stated reversal and three positions to distinguish total path length (distance) from the directed change in position (displacement), then calculates each.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.1 Distinguish distance and displacement, then calculate both for the trolley's first 6 s of motion. [8]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 10 motion in one dimension: average speed and average velocity
question_mappings.coverage_link: Calculates average velocity from signed displacement and average speed from total distance over the same time interval, then explains the directional distinction.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.2 For the first 6 s, calculate the trolley's average velocity and average speed. State one difference between them. [9]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 10 motion in one dimension: acceleration
question_mappings.coverage_link: Calculates acceleration from a change in velocity over time.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.3 Calculate acceleration during the later interval and state what its sign means. [10]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 10 motion in one dimension: constant acceleration and signed displacement from a velocity-time graph
question_mappings.coverage_link: Uses the later acceleration from Question 1.3 over a stated further 3 s, calculates final velocity, and finds signed displacement by drawing the data-based velocity-time trapezium or showing its area calculation; no pre-drawn graph is assumed.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.4 Assume the later acceleration stays constant at the value from Question 1.3 for a further 3 s, starting at +15 m·s⁻¹. Calculate the final velocity and signed displacement. Draw a velocity-time graph for this interval or show the trapezium area calculation, and state the direction. [11]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 10 motion representations and graphs
question_mappings.coverage_link: Interprets both graph axes and units, gradients, constant-position/velocity horizontal lines, and signed velocity-time area as displacement.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.5 Compare a position-time graph and a velocity-time graph. For each graph, name both axes and give their units; state what its gradient represents and what a horizontal line means. For the velocity-time graph, state what the signed area represents. [12]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 11 Term 1: reading for information and inference
question_mappings.coverage_link: Identifies the muddy, slippery route from the passage, cites its location and duration/condition after rain, and explains the safety or access reason for repair; survey-table figures are assessed separately in Question 1.3.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.1 State the route problem. Give two details showing the conditions learners faced, and explain one reason the repair mattered. [8]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 11 Term 1: infer and evaluate information
question_mappings.coverage_link: Interprets source details and explains the purpose of the environmental safeguard.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.2 Identify the two environmental choices in the club's plan and explain the purpose of each. [9]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 11 Term 2: reading visual information and proportion
question_mappings.coverage_link: Reads and compares categories in a printed survey table, calculates both proportions, and states what the figures show; the case is a source-bound visual-text exercise, not a claim that the survey represents all learners.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.3 Use the survey table to compare daily and occasional route use. Calculate the percentage in each group and write one accurate sentence describing what the figures show. [10]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 11 Term 2: critical awareness of viewpoints
question_mappings.coverage_link: Evaluates the feedback method and considers attitude, position and assumptions.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.4 Assess one strength and one limitation of the club's feedback method. [11]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 11 Term 1: informative written paragraph
question_mappings.coverage_link: Writes a coherent recommendation in an informative paragraph using evidence.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.5 Write a short recommendation to the eco-club about its next step, using evidence from the passage. [12]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Grade 12 Term 1: Macro environment — impact of recent legislation on business; Consumer Protection Act
question_mappings.coverage_link: Applies the Grade 12 Term 1 macro-environment unit on the impact of recent legislation to Koru's ingredient label, using the Consumer Protection Act and a source-based requirement to avoid misleading trade descriptions.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.1 The Consumer Protection Act is part of the Grade 12 CAPS topic on the impact of recent legislation. Using the ingredient information in the case, explain how this law could affect Koru's label decisions, state one check the owners should make before printing, and explain one possible effect of a misleading description. [8]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Human Resources function; quality of performance within business functions
question_mappings.coverage_link: Connects employee skills development and safe practice with the investment, production-capacity and product-consistency considerations in the case.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.2 Explain two different considerations before buying the drying machine. Use case details and identify a cost, sales or production estimate to check, plus one worker training or safety issue. [9]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Corporate social responsibility; Human Rights, inclusivity and environmental issues
question_mappings.coverage_link: Examines accurate product information, fair treatment of suppliers and workers, and responsible business conduct using the case context.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.3 Explain why accurate ingredient information and fair supplier relationships matter. [10]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Macro-environment business strategies
question_mappings.coverage_link: Evaluates an external sales-channel opportunity and risks, identifying information the business should investigate before choosing a response.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.4 Evaluate the supermarket offer: give one opportunity and two risks the owners should investigate. [11]

question_mappings.caps_topic: Formulation, implementation and evaluation of business strategies
question_mappings.coverage_link: Recommends whether and under what conditions the business should respond to a larger-order opportunity, using case evidence and risk controls.
question_mappings.prompt: 1.5 Recommend whether Koru should accept the offer now, delay, or negotiate conditions. Support your recommendation with evidence and two practical conditions. [12]
